title: The way of the sword
blurb: Samurai films, from Kurosawa's wandering swordsmen to a father pushing a baby cart full of blades, and a few ghosts along the way.

films.note: Kurosawa and Mifune: one swordsman plays two gangs against each other. Leone remade it as A Fistful of Dollars.
A ronin asks to die in a lord's courtyard, and takes the samurai code apart as he does.
Kurosawa turns Macbeth into a samurai film. The arrows at the end were real.
Mifune's swordsman again, and one of the most famous duels ever filmed.
A disgraced executioner, his infant son and a baby cart full of blades.
Mifune against his own clan, to keep the family he has made.
A thief is made to stand in for a dead warlord. Lucas and Coppola helped Kurosawa find the money.
Most of it was recut into Shogun Assassin for American audiences.
Shintaro Katsu as the blind swordsman nobody sees coming.
Two women murdered by samurai come back as cat spirits for revenge.
A samurai's obsession, in colour so rich it won the top prize at Cannes.
Mizoguchi's wartime telling of the most famous revenge in Japanese history.
Four ghost stories, painted rather than shot.
Two women in the reeds kill stray samurai for their armour.
Two warlords, thousands of extras in red and black.
